def issue_close(number: int, reason: str = "completed",
                comment: str | None = None) -> None:
    if reason not in ("completed", "not-planned"):
        raise LayerError(f"invalid close reason {reason!r}")
    # /issues/{n} also answers for pull requests; closing a PR through the
    # issues endpoint would bypass the merge gate's whole evidence model.
    if "pull_request" in issue_view(number):
        raise LayerError(f"#{number} is a pull request — merge it through pr_merge.py "
                         "or close it from the PR surface, never via issue_close")
    if comment:
        ensure_pr_comment(number, f"<!-- mipstarre-close-note-{number} -->", comment)
    api(f"issues/{number}", method="PATCH",
        payload={"state": "closed",
                 "state_reason": "not_planned" if reason == "not-planned" else reason},
        mutation=True, idempotent=True)

def snapshot(out_dir: Path) -> None:
    issues = [r for r in api("issues?state=open", paginate=True)
              if "pull_request" not in r]
    pulls = api("pulls?state=open", paginate=True)
    meta = {"generated": utcnow(), "repo": repo_slug(),
            "open_issues": len(issues), "open_pulls": len(pulls)}
    out = Path(out_dir)
    atomic_write(out / "open-issues.json", json.dumps(issues, indent=1) + "\n")
    atomic_write(out / "open-pulls.json", json.dumps(pulls, indent=1) + "\n")
    atomic_write(out / "metadata.json", json.dumps(meta, indent=1) + "\n")

open Lake DSL System

package proofwidgets where

def widgetDir : FilePath := "widget"

nonrec def Lake.Package.widgetDir (pkg : Package) : FilePath :=
  pkg.dir / widgetDir

def Lake.Package.runNpmCommand (pkg : Package) (args : Array String) : LogIO Unit :=
  -- Running `cmd := "npm.cmd"` directly fails on Windows sometimes
  -- (https://github.com/leanprover-community/ProofWidgets4/issues/97)
  -- so run in PowerShell instead (`cmd.exe` also doesn't work.)
  if Platform.isWindows then
    proc {
      cmd := "powershell"
      args := #["-Command", "npm.cmd"] ++ args
      cwd := some pkg.widgetDir
    } (quiet := true) -- use `quiet` here or `lake` will replay the output in downstream projects.
  else
    proc {
      cmd := "npm"
      args
      cwd := some pkg.widgetDir
    } (quiet := true)

input_file widgetPackageJson where
  path := widgetDir / "package.json"
  text := true

/-- Target to update `package-lock.json` whenever `package.json` has changed. -/
target widgetPackageLock pkg : FilePath := do
  let packageFile ← widgetPackageJson.fetch
  let packageLockFile := pkg.widgetDir / "package-lock.json"
  buildFileAfterDep (text := true) packageLockFile packageFile fun _srcFile => do

    32	/-- Parameters for the `(m,q,d)` low individual degree test.
    33	
    34	Besides the usual positivity assumptions, we bundle the paper-faithful witness
    35	that `q = p^n` is a prime power. -/
    36	structure Parameters where
    37	  m : ℕ
    38	  q : ℕ
    39	  d : ℕ
    40	  hm : 0 < m
    41	  /-- Kept as a compatibility field so existing positivity proofs can continue
    42	  to use `params.hq`; it is derivable from `hqPrimePower`. -/
    43	  hq : 0 < q
    44	  /-- Paper-faithful witness that `q` is a prime power. -/
    45	  hqPrimePower : ∃ p n, Nat.Prime p ∧ 0 < n ∧ q = p ^ n

    49	namespace Parameters

    51	/-- Any number presented as a prime power is automatically positive. -/
    52	theorem q_pos_of_primePower {q : ℕ}
    53	    (hqPrimePower : ∃ p n, Nat.Prime p ∧ 0 < n ∧ q = p ^ n) : 0 < q := by
    54	  rcases hqPrimePower with ⟨p, n, hp, hn, rfl⟩
    55	  exact Nat.pow_pos hp.pos
    56	
    57	/-- Prime numbers are prime powers of exponent `1`. -/
    58	theorem prime_primePower {q : ℕ} (hqPrime : Nat.Prime q) :
    59	    ∃ p n, Nat.Prime p ∧ 0 < n ∧ q = p ^ n := by
    60	  exact ⟨q, 1, hqPrime, by decide, by simp⟩
    61	
    62	/-- Build parameters from explicit prime-power data `q = p^n`. -/
    63	def ofPrimePower (m q d p n : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) (hp : Nat.Prime p) (hn : 0 < n)
    64	    (hq : q = p ^ n) : Parameters :=
    65	  { m := m
    66	    q := q
    67	    d := d
    68	    hm := hm
    69	    hq := q_pos_of_primePower ⟨p, n, hp, hn, hq⟩
    70	    hqPrimePower := ⟨p, n, hp, hn, hq⟩ }
    71	
    72	/-- Build parameters when `q` itself is prime. -/
    73	def ofPrime (m q d : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) (hqPrime : Nat.Prime q) : Parameters :=
    74	  { m := m
    75	    q := q
    76	    d := d
    77	    hm := hm
    78	    hq := hqPrime.pos
    79	    hqPrimePower := prime_primePower hqPrime }

    81	/-- Convenience constructor for the ubiquitous binary field. -/
    82	def ofTwo (m d : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) : Parameters :=
    83	  ofPrime m 2 d hm Nat.prime_two
    84	
    85	/-- Paper finite fields have at least two elements: `q = p^n` with `p` prime
    86	and `0 < n` (see `preliminaries.tex`, lines 17--19 and 89--93). -/
    87	theorem two_le_q (params : Parameters) : 2 ≤ params.q := by
    88	  obtain ⟨p, n, hp, hn, hq⟩ := params.hqPrimePower
    89	  rw [hq]
    90	  exact le_trans hp.two_le (Nat.le_self_pow (Nat.ne_of_gt hn) p)
    91	
    92	/-- The field-size parameter is strictly larger than `1`. -/
    93	theorem one_lt_q (params : Parameters) : 1 < params.q :=
    94	  lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.one_lt_two params.two_le_q
    95	
    96	/-- Positivity of the field-size parameter after casting to the repository's
    97	real-valued error scalar type. -/
    98	theorem q_cast_pos (params : Parameters) : 0 < (params.q : Error) :=
    99	  Nat.cast_pos.mpr params.hq

   106	/-- The successor test obtained by appending one coordinate. -/
   107	def Parameters.next (params : Parameters) : Parameters :=
   108	  { m := params.m + 1
   109	    q := params.q

   117	/-- The predecessor parameters obtained by removing the last coordinate from a
   118	non-base ambient dimension.
   119	
   120	This is the inverse construction to `Parameters.next` on the data fields.  The
   121	proof fields are inherited from the original parameter bundle, so the inverse is
   122	propositional rather than definitional. -/
   123	def previous (params : Parameters) (hm : 1 < params.m) : Parameters :=
   124	  { m := params.m - 1
   125	    q := params.q
   126	    d := params.d
   127	    hm := Nat.sub_pos_of_lt hm
   128	    hq := params.hq
   129	    hqPrimePower := params.hqPrimePower }
   130	
   131	/-- Removing the last coordinate and then applying `Parameters.next` recovers the
   132	original non-base parameters. -/
   133	theorem previous_next_eq (params : Parameters) (hm : 1 < params.m) :
   134	    (previous params hm).next = params := by
   135	  cases params with
   136	  | mk m q d hm0 hq hqPrimePower =>
   137	      have hsub : m - 1 + 1 = m := Nat.sub_add_cancel (le_of_lt hm)
   138	      simp [previous, Parameters.next, hsub]
   139	
   140	/-- A bundled predecessor for a parameter set known to be a successor dimension. -/
   141	structure SuccessorDecomposition (params : Parameters) where
   142	  /-- The predecessor parameter bundle. -/
   143	  pred : Parameters
   144	  /-- The predecessor's successor is the original parameter bundle. -/
   145	  next_eq : pred.next = params
   146	
   147	/-- Every parameter bundle of dimension strictly larger than one has a bundled
   148	predecessor whose successor is propositionally equal to the original bundle. -/
   149	def successorDecompositionOfOneLtM (params : Parameters) (hm : 1 < params.m) :
   150	    SuccessorDecomposition params where
   151	  pred := previous params hm
   152	  next_eq := previous_next_eq params hm
   153	
   154	/-- A positive dimension that is not the base dimension is strictly larger than
   155	one. -/
   156	theorem one_lt_m_of_ne_one (params : Parameters) (hm_ne_one : params.m ≠ 1) :
   157	    1 < params.m :=
   158	  lt_of_le_of_ne params.hm (Ne.symm hm_ne_one)

   160	/-- Non-base parameters have a bundled predecessor decomposition. -/
   161	def successorDecompositionOfNeOne (params : Parameters) (hm_ne_one : params.m ≠ 1) :
   162	    SuccessorDecomposition params :=
   163	  successorDecompositionOfOneLtM params (one_lt_m_of_ne_one params hm_ne_one)

   210	/-- A bundled field model for the paper's `F_q`, together with a coding equivalence
   211	to the repository's finite carrier `Fin q`. -/
   212	class FieldModel (q : ℕ) where
   213	  K : Type*
   214	  instField : Field K
   215	  instFintype : Fintype K

   224	/-- The carrier bundled in a `FieldModel q` has exactly `q` elements, matching the

   226	@[simp] theorem card (q : ℕ) [FieldModel q] :
   227	    Fintype.card (FieldModel.K q) = q := by
   228	  simpa using Fintype.card_congr (FieldModel.equiv (q := q))

   230	/-- A bundled field model has a nonempty finite carrier. -/

   232	    0 < Fintype.card (FieldModel.K q) :=
   233	  Fintype.card_pos_iff.mpr ⟨0⟩

   235	/-- The finite cardinality of a bundled field model is nonzero. -/
   236	theorem card_ne_zero (q : ℕ) [FieldModel q] :

   242	/-- Build the honest field model from prime-power data. -/
   243	@[reducible] noncomputable def PrimePowerFieldSpec.toFieldModel (params : Parameters)
   244	    (spec : PrimePowerFieldSpec params) : FieldModel params.q := by
   245	  classical
   246	  letI : Fact spec.p.Prime := ⟨spec.pPrime⟩
   247	  let K := HonestFq params spec
   248	  letI : Fintype K := Fintype.ofFinite K
   249	  have hcard : Fintype.card K = params.q := by
   250	    rw [← Nat.card_eq_fintype_card, spec.cardEq]
   251	    simpa [K, HonestFq] using (GaloisField.card (p := spec.p) (n := spec.n) spec.nPos.ne')
   252	  exact
   253	    { K := K
   254	      instField := inferInstance
   255	      instFintype := inferInstance
   256	      instDecidableEq := inferInstance
   257	      equiv := Fintype.equivFinOfCardEq hcard }

     3	/-!
     4	# The combining map on tuples of low individual degree polynomials
     5	
     6	The extension of the quantum soundness of the low individual degree test from
     7	simultaneity parameter `1` to a general simultaneity parameter `k` is obtained
     8	in the source by a reduction, not coordinatewise: the `k` answer polynomials
     9	`g_0, …, g_{k-1}` in `m` variables are combined into the single polynomial
    10	
    11	`comb(g)(u, α) = ∑_{r < k} α_r g_r(u)`
    12	
    13	in `m + k` variables, the case `k = 1` is applied once in dimension `m + k`,
    14	and the `k` polynomials are recovered from the resulting outcome by exact
    15	linearity in the combining variables `α` together with the Schwartz--Zippel
    16	lemma.  This module develops the polynomial algebra of that combining map: the
    17	coordinate split of `Fin (m + k)`, the map itself, its evaluation identity, its
    18	individual-degree bound, and the substitution recovering the `r`-th component,
    19	which exhibits the map as injective.
    20	
    21	The combining map of `def:combine-map` (`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Defs.lean`)
    22	is the special case of two components used by the Chapter 15 combining
    23	argument, written there in the fixed coordinate layout of that chapter; the
    24	present map is the general `k`-component form required by the reduction, in the
    25	coordinate layout of the directly indexed low-degree game, where the `m` point
    26	coordinates precede the `k` combining coordinates.
    27	
    28	## Main definitions
    29	
    30	* `combinedPointVar`, `combinedCoefficientVar` — the two coordinate blocks of
    31	  the combined dimension `m + k`.
    32	* `combinePolyTuple` — the combining map on tuples of polynomials.
    33	* `splitCombinedPoly` — the substitution `α ↦ e_r` recovering the `r`-th
    34	  component of a combined polynomial.
    35	
    36	## References
    37	
    38	* `references/neexp-paper/05_quantum_preliminaries.tex:1409-1503`
    39	  (the derivation of Theorem 4.43 from Theorem 4.40)
    40	* `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:413-458`
    41	* `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:240-250`
    42	* `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-simultaneous-sandwich.tex`
    43	-/
    44	
    45	open scoped BigOperators
    46	
    47	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    48	
    49	open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    50	
    51	noncomputable section
    52	
    53	/-! ## The coordinates of the combined dimension -/
    54	
    55	/-- The point coordinates of the combined dimension `m + k`.  The `m` point
    56	coordinates come first, so that zeroing a prefix of a direction of the combined
    57	space restricts to zeroing the corresponding prefix of its point part. -/
    58	def combinedPointVar (m k : ℕ) (j : Fin m) : Fin (m + k) :=
    59	  finSumFinEquiv (Sum.inl j)
    60	
    61	/-- The combining coordinates of the combined dimension `m + k`.  Coordinate
    62	`combinedCoefficientVar m k r` carries the scalar `α_r` multiplying the `r`-th
    63	component of a polynomial tuple. -/
    64	def combinedCoefficientVar (m k : ℕ) (r : Fin k) : Fin (m + k) :=
    65	  finSumFinEquiv (Sum.inr r)
    66	
    67	theorem combinedPointVar_injective (m k : ℕ) :
    68	    Function.Injective (combinedPointVar m k) := by
    69	  intro j j' h
    70	  simpa using finSumFinEquiv.injective h
    71	
    72	theorem combinedCoefficientVar_injective (m k : ℕ) :
    73	    Function.Injective (combinedCoefficientVar m k) := by
    74	  intro r r' h
    75	  simpa using finSumFinEquiv.injective h
    76	
    77	/-- The two coordinate blocks of the combined dimension are disjoint. -/
    78	theorem combinedCoefficientVar_ne_combinedPointVar (m k : ℕ) (r : Fin k) (j : Fin m) :
    79	    combinedCoefficientVar m k r ≠ combinedPointVar m k j := by
    80	  intro h
    81	  have := finSumFinEquiv.injective h
    82	  simp at this
    83	
    84	theorem combinedCoefficientVar_notMem_range (m k : ℕ) (r : Fin k) :
    85	    combinedCoefficientVar m k r ∉ Set.range (combinedPointVar m k) := by
    86	  rintro ⟨j, hj⟩
    87	  exact combinedCoefficientVar_ne_combinedPointVar m k r j hj.symm
    88	
    89	/-- The point part of a point of the combined space. -/
    90	def combinedPointPart {K : Type*} {m k : ℕ} (z : Fin (m + k) → K) : Fin m → K :=
    91	  fun j => z (combinedPointVar m k j)
    92	
    93	/-- The combining part of a point of the combined space. -/
    94	def combinedCoefficientPart {K : Type*} {m k : ℕ} (z : Fin (m + k) → K) : Fin k → K :=
    95	  fun r => z (combinedCoefficientVar m k r)
    96	
    97	/-- The point of the combined space with the given point and combining parts. -/
    98	def combinedPoint {K : Type*} {m k : ℕ} (u : Fin m → K) (α : Fin k → K) :
    99	    Fin (m + k) → K :=
   100	  fun i => Sum.elim u α (finSumFinEquiv.symm i)
   101	
   102	@[simp] theorem combinedPointPart_combinedPoint {K : Type*} {m k : ℕ}
   103	    (u : Fin m → K) (α : Fin k → K) :
   104	    combinedPointPart (combinedPoint u α) = u := by
   105	  funext j
   106	  simp [combinedPointPart, combinedPoint, combinedPointVar]
   107	
   108	@[simp] theorem combinedCoefficientPart_combinedPoint {K : Type*} {m k : ℕ}
   109	    (u : Fin m → K) (α : Fin k → K) :
   110	    combinedCoefficientPart (combinedPoint u α) = α := by
   111	  funext r
   112	  simp [combinedCoefficientPart, combinedPoint, combinedCoefficientVar]
   113	
   114	/-! ## The combining map -/
   115	
   116	/-- The combining map of the reduction: the tuple `g` is sent to the polynomial
   117	`(u, α) ↦ ∑_{r < k} α_r g_r(u)` in `m + k` variables.
   118	
   119	Source `references/neexp-paper/05_quantum_preliminaries.tex:1425-1435`. -/
   120	def combinePolyTuple {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {m k : ℕ}
   121	    (g : Fin k → MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) : MvPolynomial (Fin (m + k)) K :=
   122	  ∑ r : Fin k, MvPolynomial.X (combinedCoefficientVar m k r) *
   123	    MvPolynomial.rename (combinedPointVar m k) (g r)
   124	
   125	/-- Evaluation of a combined polynomial is the displayed combining formula. -/
   126	theorem combinePolyTuple_eval {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {m k : ℕ}
   127	    (g : Fin k → MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) (z : Fin (m + k) → K) :
   128	    MvPolynomial.eval z (combinePolyTuple g) =
   129	      ∑ r : Fin k, combinedCoefficientPart z r *
   130	        MvPolynomial.eval (combinedPointPart z) (g r) := by
   131	  simp only [combinePolyTuple, map_sum, map_mul, MvPolynomial.eval_X,
   132	    MvPolynomial.eval_rename, combinedCoefficientPart]
   133	  rfl
   134	
   135	/-- Evaluation of a combined polynomial at a point given by its two blocks. -/
   136	theorem combinePolyTuple_eval_combinedPoint {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {m k : ℕ}
   137	    (g : Fin k → MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) (u : Fin m → K) (α : Fin k → K) :
   138	    MvPolynomial.eval (combinedPoint u α) (combinePolyTuple g) =
   139	      ∑ r : Fin k, α r * MvPolynomial.eval u (g r) := by
   140	  rw [combinePolyTuple_eval, combinedPointPart_combinedPoint,
   141	    combinedCoefficientPart_combinedPoint]
   142	
   143	/-! ## Recovering the components -/
   144	
   145	/-- The substitution sending each point coordinate to its own variable and the
   146	combining coordinates to the `r`-th standard basis vector.  Applied to a
   147	combined polynomial it returns the `r`-th component of the tuple. -/
   148	def combinedSubstitution (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K] (m k : ℕ) (r : Fin k) :
   149	    Fin (m + k) → MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=
   150	  fun i => Sum.elim (fun j : Fin m => MvPolynomial.X j)
   151	    (fun s : Fin k => if s = r then 1 else 0) (finSumFinEquiv.symm i)
   152	
   153	@[simp] theorem combinedSubstitution_point (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K] (m k : ℕ)
   154	    (r : Fin k) (j : Fin m) :
   155	    combinedSubstitution K m k r (combinedPointVar m k j) = MvPolynomial.X j := by
   156	  simp [combinedSubstitution, combinedPointVar]
   157	
   158	@[simp] theorem combinedSubstitution_coefficient (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K] (m k : ℕ)
   159	    (r s : Fin k) :
   160	    combinedSubstitution K m k r (combinedCoefficientVar m k s) =
   161	      if s = r then 1 else 0 := by
   162	  simp [combinedSubstitution, combinedCoefficientVar]
   163	
   164	/-- The `r`-th component of a polynomial in the combined variables: substitute
   165	the `r`-th standard basis vector for the combining variables. -/
   166	def splitCombinedPoly {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {m k : ℕ}
   167	    (p : MvPolynomial (Fin (m + k)) K) (r : Fin k) : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=
   168	  MvPolynomial.aeval (combinedSubstitution K m k r) p
   169	
   170	/-- The components of a combined polynomial are the polynomials it combines. -/
   171	theorem splitCombinedPoly_combinePolyTuple {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {m k : ℕ}
   172	    (g : Fin k → MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) (r : Fin k) :
   173	    splitCombinedPoly (combinePolyTuple g) r = g r := by
   174	  classical
   175	  have hcomp : (combinedSubstitution K m k r) ∘ (combinedPointVar m k) =
   176	      (MvPolynomial.X : Fin m → MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) := by
   177	    funext j
   178	    exact combinedSubstitution_point K m k r j
   179	  have hterm : ∀ s : Fin k,
   180	      MvPolynomial.aeval (combinedSubstitution K m k r)
   181	          (MvPolynomial.X (combinedCoefficientVar m k s) *
   182	            MvPolynomial.rename (combinedPointVar m k) (g s)) =
   183	        (if s = r then 1 else 0) * g s := by
   184	    intro s
   185	    rw [map_mul, MvPolynomial.aeval_X, combinedSubstitution_coefficient,
   186	      MvPolynomial.aeval_rename, hcomp, MvPolynomial.aeval_X_left_apply]
   187	  rw [splitCombinedPoly, combinePolyTuple, map_sum]
   188	  simp only [hterm, ite_mul, one_mul, zero_mul]
   189	  simp
   190	
   191	/-- The combining map is injective: the components of a combined polynomial are
   192	determined by it. -/
   193	theorem combinePolyTuple_injective {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {m k : ℕ} :
   194	    Function.Injective (combinePolyTuple (K := K) (m := m) (k := k)) := by
   195	  intro g g' h
   196	  funext r
   197	  rw [← splitCombinedPoly_combinePolyTuple g r, h,
   198	    splitCombinedPoly_combinePolyTuple]

   201	
   202	/-- Membership in the low individual degree class from a bound on every
   203	individual degree.  This is the converse direction of
   204	`degreeOf_le_of_mem_polyFunc`. -/
   205	theorem mem_polyFunc_of_degreeOf_le {m d : ℕ} {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K]
   206	    {p : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K} (h : ∀ i, p.degreeOf i ≤ d) :
   207	    p ∈ polyFunc m K d := by
   208	  rw [MvPolynomial.mem_restrictDegree]
   209	  exact fun s hs i => MvPolynomial.degreeOf_le_iff.mp (h i) s hs

   223	private theorem degreeOf_rename_le {σ τ K : Type*} [CommSemiring K]
   224	    {f : σ → τ} (hf : Function.Injective f) {p : MvPolynomial σ K} {d : ℕ}
   225	    (hp : ∀ j : σ, p.degreeOf j ≤ d) (i : τ) :
   226	    (MvPolynomial.rename f p).degreeOf i ≤ d := by
   227	  classical
   228	  rw [MvPolynomial.degreeOf_le_iff]
   229	  intro s hs
   230	  rw [MvPolynomial.support_rename_of_injective hf] at hs
   231	  obtain ⟨t, ht, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hs
   232	  by_cases hi : ∃ j, f j = i
   233	  · obtain ⟨j, rfl⟩ := hi
   234	    rw [Finsupp.mapDomain_apply hf]
   235	    exact le_trans (MvPolynomial.le_degreeOf_of_mem_support j ht) (hp j)
   236	  · rw [Finsupp.mapDomain_notin_range t i (by simpa using hi)]
   237	    exact Nat.zero_le d
   238	
   239	private theorem degreeOf_rename_eq_zero_of_notMem_range {σ τ K : Type*} [CommSemiring K]
   240	    {f : σ → τ} (hf : Function.Injective f) (p : MvPolynomial σ K)
   241	    {i : τ} (hi : i ∉ Set.range f) :
   242	    (MvPolynomial.rename f p).degreeOf i = 0 := by
   243	  classical
   244	  rw [← Nat.le_zero, MvPolynomial.degreeOf_le_iff]
   245	  intro s hs
   246	  rw [MvPolynomial.support_rename_of_injective hf] at hs
   247	  obtain ⟨t, _, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hs
   248	  exact le_of_eq (Finsupp.mapDomain_notin_range t i hi)
   249	
   250	/-- The combining map preserves the individual-degree bound.  The two coordinate
   251	blocks are disjoint: a component polynomial depends only on the point
   252	coordinates, so multiplying it by a combining variable leaves its individual
   253	degrees in the point block unchanged and produces individual degree one in the
   254	fresh combining coordinate.  The hypothesis `1 ≤ d` supplies exactly the bound
   255	needed on that fresh coordinate; no bound `d + 1` is introduced.  This is the
   256	individual-degree counterpart of the degree-`d + 1` bound used for total degree
   257	in `references/neexp-paper/05_quantum_preliminaries.tex:1435-1440`. -/
   258	theorem combinePolyTuple_mem_polyFunc {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {m k d : ℕ}
   259	    (hd : 1 ≤ d) (g : Fin k → MvPolynomial (Fin m) K)
   260	    (hg : ∀ r, g r ∈ polyFunc m K d) :
   261	    combinePolyTuple g ∈ polyFunc (m + k) K d := by
   262	  classical
   263	  refine Submodule.sum_mem _ fun r _ => mem_polyFunc_of_degreeOf_le fun i => ?_
   264	  refine le_trans (MvPolynomial.degreeOf_mul_le i _ _) ?_
   265	  by_cases hi : i ∈ Set.range (combinedPointVar m k)
   266	  · have hne : i ≠ combinedCoefficientVar m k r := by
   267	      rintro rfl
   268	      exact combinedCoefficientVar_notMem_range m k r hi
   269	    rw [MvPolynomial.degreeOf_X_of_ne hne, zero_add]
   270	    exact degreeOf_rename_le (combinedPointVar_injective m k)
   271	      (fun j => degreeOf_le_of_mem_polyFunc (hg r) j) i
   272	  · rw [degreeOf_rename_eq_zero_of_notMem_range (combinedPointVar_injective m k) _ hi,
   273	      add_zero]
   274	    exact le_trans (degreeOf_X_le_one _ _) hd
   275	
   276	end
   277	
   278	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

lemma fourierBasisState_total_update_sum (params : Parameters) (u α : Point params) :
    ∑ i : Fin params.m, ∑ x : Fq params, fourierBasisState params α (Function.update u i x) =
      ((((params.m - frequencyWeight params α : ℕ) : ℂ) * (params.q : ℂ)) *
        fourierBasisState params α u) := by
  calc
    ∑ i : Fin params.m, ∑ x : Fq params, fourierBasisState params α (Function.update u i x)
      = ∑ i : Fin params.m,
          (((if α i = (0 : Fq params) then params.q else 0 : ℕ) : ℂ) *
            fourierBasisState params α u) := by
              congr 1 with i
              exact fourierBasisState_update_sum params u α i
    _ = (∑ i : Fin params.m,
          (((if α i = (0 : Fq params) then params.q else 0 : ℕ) : ℂ))) *
          fourierBasisState params α u := by
            rw [Finset.sum_mul]
    _ = ((((params.m - frequencyWeight params α : ℕ) : ℂ) * (params.q : ℂ)) *
          fourierBasisState params α u) := by
            rw [zeroCoordinateContributionSum]

/-- The actual inner product of two Fourier basis states on `ℂ^{F_q^m}`.

Since `fourierBasisState` already includes the `1 / √M` normalization, this is
just the finite sum `∑_u conj(φ_α(u)) * φ_β(u)`. -/
noncomputable def fourierBasisInnerProduct (params : Parameters)
    (α β : Point params) : ℂ :=
  ∑ u : Point params, star (fourierBasisState params α u) * fourierBasisState params β u

/-- The additive character on `Point params` indexed by a frequency `α`. -/
noncomputable def pointAddChar (params : Parameters) (α : Point params) :
    AddChar (Point params) ℂ where
  toFun u := ZMod.stdAddChar (N := params.q) (dotProductZMod params u α)
  map_zero_eq_one' := by
    simp [dotProductZMod]
  map_add_eq_mul' := by
    intro u v
    have hdot :
        dotProductZMod params (u + v) α =
          dotProductZMod params u α + dotProductZMod params v α := by
      unfold dotProductZMod
      calc
        ∑ i, (((u + v) i).val : ZMod params.q) * ((α i).val : ZMod params.q)
          = ∑ i,
              ((((u i).val : ZMod params.q) + ((v i).val : ZMod params.q)) *
                ((α i).val : ZMod params.q)) := by
                  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
                  intro i _
                  have hcast :
                      ((((u + v) i).val : ZMod params.q)) =
                        ((u i).val : ZMod params.q) + ((v i).val : ZMod params.q) := by
                    simp [Fin.val_add]
                  rw [hcast]
        _ = ∑ i,
              (((u i).val : ZMod params.q) * ((α i).val : ZMod params.q) +
                ((v i).val : ZMod params.q) * ((α i).val : ZMod params.q)) := by
                  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
                  intro i _
                  ring
        _ = dotProductZMod params u α + dotProductZMod params v α := by
              simp [dotProductZMod, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    rw [hdot, AddChar.map_add_eq_mul]

/-- The additive character on the frequency space obtained by fixing a point `u`. -/
noncomputable def pointAddCharRight (params : Parameters) (u : Point params) :
    AddChar (Point params) ℂ where
  toFun α := ZMod.stdAddChar (N := params.q) (dotProductZMod params u α)
  map_zero_eq_one' := by
    simp [dotProductZMod]
  map_add_eq_mul' := by
    intro α β
    have hdot :
        dotProductZMod params u (α + β) =
          dotProductZMod params u α + dotProductZMod params u β := by
      unfold dotProductZMod
      calc
        ∑ i, ((u i).val : ZMod params.q) * (((α + β) i).val : ZMod params.q)
          = ∑ i,
              apply (pointAddChar_eq_zero_iff params (β - α)).2
              simp [hab]
            simp [h0, hab]

/-- `prop:eigenvectors`, item 1: orthonormality of the Fourier basis. -/
lemma eigenvectors_orthonormality (params : Parameters) (α β : Point params) :
    fourierBasisInnerProduct params α β = if α = β then 1 else 0 := by
  simpa [fourierBasisInnerProduct] using fourierBasisState_inner_product params α β

/-- The eigenvalue of `K` on `φ_α`. -/
noncomputable def adjacencyEigenvalue (params : Parameters) (α : Point params) : Error :=
  (1 / (hypercubeVertexCount params : Error)) *
    (((params.m - frequencyWeight params α : ℕ) : Error) / (params.m : Error))

/-- The eigenvalue of `L` on `φ_α`. -/
noncomputable def laplacianEigenvalue (params : Parameters) (α : Point params) : Error :=
  (frequencyWeight params α : Error) /
    ((params.m : Error) * (hypercubeVertexCount params : Error))

/-- The spectral gap `1 / (m M)` from `cor:laplacian-spectral-gap`. -/
noncomputable def hypercubeSpectralGap (params : Parameters) : Error :=
  1 / ((params.m : Error) * (hypercubeVertexCount params : Error))

/-- The Fourier index set `F_q^m` has cardinality `M = q^m`. -/
lemma eigenvectors_card (params : Parameters) :
    Fintype.card (Point params) = hypercubeVertexCount params := by
  simp [hypercubeVertexCount, Fintype.card_fin]

/-- `prop:eigenvectors`, item 2: each `|φ_α⟩` is an eigenvector of the
adjacency matrix `K` with eigenvalue `λ_α`. -/
theorem eigenvectors (params : Parameters) (α : Point params) :
    (matrixAdjacencyOperator params).mulVec (fourierBasisState params α) =
      ((adjacencyEigenvalue params α : ℝ) : ℂ) • fourierBasisState params α := by
  ext u
  let c : ℂ := (((params.m : ℂ) * (params.q : ℂ) * (hypercubeVertexCount params : ℂ))⁻¹)
  have hmul :
      (matrixAdjacencyOperator params).mulVec (fourierBasisState params α) u =
        c * ∑ i : Fin params.m, ∑ x : Fq params,
          fourierBasisState params α (Function.update u i x) := by

      (matrixAdjacencyOperator params).mulVec (fourierBasisState params α) u

              change ∑ v : Point params,

/-- Restrict a global polynomial in `m + 1` variables to the slice at height `x`. -/
noncomputable def restrictAtHeight (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]
    (g : Polynomial params.next) (x : Fq params) : Polynomial params where
  poly := MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom MvPolynomial.C (restrictAtHeightCoordinateMap params x) g.poly
  lowIndividualDegree := degreeOf_eval₂Hom_restrictAtHeightCoordinateMap_le params g x

/-- Coordinate polynomial for restricting to an axis-parallel affine line. -/
noncomputable def axisCoordinatePolynomial (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]
    (ℓ : AxisParallelLine params) :
    Fin params.m → LinePolynomialModel params :=
  fun i =>
    if i = ℓ.direction then
      _root_.Polynomial.C (decodeScalar (ℓ.base i)) + _root_.Polynomial.X
    else
      _root_.Polynomial.C (decodeScalar (ℓ.base i))

private theorem natDegree_axisCoordinatePolynomial_le (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]
    (ℓ : AxisParallelLine params) (i : Fin params.m) :
    (axisCoordinatePolynomial params ℓ i).natDegree ≤ if i = ℓ.direction then 1 else 0 := by
  classical
  by_cases hi : i = ℓ.direction
  · subst hi
    rcases subsingleton_or_nontrivial (Scalar params) with hsub | hnontriv
    · letI := hsub
      have hX : (_root_.Polynomial.X : LinePolynomialModel params) = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
      simp [axisCoordinatePolynomial, hX]
    · letI := hnontriv
      simp [axisCoordinatePolynomial, add_comm]
  · simp [axisCoordinatePolynomial, hi, Polynomial.natDegree_C]

/-- Restricting a low-degree polynomial to an axis-parallel line via `eval₂Hom` yields a

theorem natDegree_eval₂Hom_axisCoordinatePolynomial_le

      g.poly).natDegree ≤ params.d := by

    rw [g.poly.as_sum, map_sum]
    refine Polynomial.natDegree_sum_le_of_forall_le
      (s := g.poly.support)
      (f := fun n =>
        MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom _root_.Polynomial.C (axisCoordinatePolynomial params ℓ)
          (MvPolynomial.monomial n (g.poly.coeff n)))
      (n := params.d) ?_
    intro n hn
    rw [MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom_monomial]
    calc
      ((_root_.Polynomial.C (g.poly.coeff n) : LinePolynomialModel params) *
          ∏ j ∈ n.support, axisCoordinatePolynomial params ℓ j ^ n j).natDegree ≤
          (∏ j ∈ n.support, axisCoordinatePolynomial params ℓ j ^ n j).natDegree :=
        Polynomial.natDegree_C_mul_le _ _
      _ ≤ ∑ j ∈ n.support, (axisCoordinatePolynomial params ℓ j ^ n j).natDegree :=
        Polynomial.natDegree_prod_le _ _
      _ ≤ ∑ j ∈ n.support, if j = ℓ.direction then n j else 0 := by
      _ ≤ ∑ j ∈ n.support, if j = ℓ.direction then n j else 0 := by

        intro j hj

@[simp] theorem restrictToAxisParallelLine_apply
    (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]
    (g : Polynomial params) (ℓ : AxisParallelLine params) (t : Fq params) :
    restrictToAxisParallelLine params g ℓ t = g (ℓ.pointAt t) := by

      (Polynomial.eval (decodeScalar t)

          (axisCoordinatePolynomial params ℓ) g.poly)) = _

        (fun s => Polynomial.eval (decodeScalar t)

# Section 7 — Matrix realization

This file gives concrete finite-dimensional matrix realizations of the
hypercube variance operators, Fourier projectors, and spectral inequalities
introduced in `Defs`.

## References

- `blueprint/src/chapter/ch05_expansion.tex`
- `references/ldt-paper/expansion.tex`

namespace MIPStarRE.LDT.ExpansionHypercubeGraph

open MIPStarRE.LDT
open MIPStarRE.LDT.MakingMeasurementsProjective
open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder

universe u

/-- Tensor two finite Hilbert spaces by taking the cartesian product of indices. -/
def tensorHilbertSpace (H K : FiniteHilbertSpace) : FiniteHilbertSpace where
  carrier := H.carrier × K.carrier
  instFintype := inferInstance
  instDecidableEq := inferInstance
  instNonempty := inferInstance

/-- Kronecker product of two concrete operators. -/
def matrixTensorOperator {H K : FiniteHilbertSpace}
    (A : MatrixOperator H) (B : MatrixOperator K) :
    MatrixOperator (tensorHilbertSpace H K) :=
  Matrix.kronecker A B

/-- Rectangular operators from `H` into `K`, represented as concrete matrices. -/
abbrev RectangularMatrixOperator (H K : FiniteHilbertSpace) :=
  Matrix K.carrier H.carrier ℂ

/-- The concrete matrix family underlying the variance calculations. -/
structure MatrixOperatorFamilyRealization (params : Parameters) where
  space : FiniteHilbertSpace.{u}
  state : PositiveMatrixState space
  family : Point params → MatrixOperator space

/-- The Section 7.1 edge distribution used by the matrix model. -/
noncomputable def matrixHypercubeEdgeDistribution (params : Parameters) :
    Distribution (Point params × Point params) :=
  rerandomizeCoord params

/-- The normalized all-ones projector onto the constant mode. -/
noncomputable def constantModeProjectorMatrix (params : Parameters) :
    MatrixOperator (pointHilbertSpace params) :=
  fun _ _ => (hypercubeVertexCount params : ℂ)⁻¹

/-- The projector onto the orthogonal complement of the constant mode. -/
noncomputable def orthogonalModeProjectorMatrix (params : Parameters) :
    MatrixOperator (pointHilbertSpace params) :=
  1 - constantModeProjectorMatrix params

private lemma fourierBasisState_apply_comm (params : Parameters) (α u : Point params) :

    addCharFq_dotProduct_eq_stdAddChar_dotProductZMod, hdot]

private lemma fourierBasisState_inner_product_dual (params : Parameters) (u v : Point params) :
    ∑ α : Point params,

        if u = v then 1 else 0 := by
  conv_lhs =>
    arg 2; ext α
    rw [fourierBasisState_apply_comm params α u, fourierBasisState_apply_comm params α v]
  exact fourierBasisState_inner_product params u v

    intro α _
    simp [fourierBasisProjector, Matrix.vecMulVec_apply]; ring
